name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, Moon, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  version:
    description: 'Version tag of Callisto to install'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        targets: wasm32-wasip1
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install Moon
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      run: |
        # Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
        # tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
        # "git add -A").
        CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
        mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
        TAG_NAME="${{ inputs.version || 'latest' }}"

        # Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
        OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
        ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)

        if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
          if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "arm64" ]]; then
            ASSET_NAME="callisto-macos-aarch64.tar.gz"
          else
            ASSET_NAME="callisto-macos-amd64.tar.gz"
          fi
        elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == "linux" ]]; then
          ASSET_NAME="callisto-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
        elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == *"mingw"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"msys"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"windows"* ]]; then
          ASSET_NAME="callisto-windows-amd64.zip"
        else
          ASSET_NAME="callisto-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
        fi

        if [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]]; then
          DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/latest/download/$ASSET_NAME"
        else
          DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/$TAG_NAME/$ASSET_NAME"
        fi
[/external_agent_tool_result]

context:

Confirmed — it was fixed on crates.io but the CI action doesn't know that. callisto-cli@0.5.0 was published to crates.io at 2026-08-27T02:58, hours before the CI run that still failed at 21:05. The dependency conflict was presumably resolved in that publish. But setup-callisto/action.yml (in orin-dx/callisto) never tries crates.io — it only:

1. checks if it's building callisto's own monorepo locally,
2. tries downloading a GitHub Release binary tarball (which doesn't exist — no assets attached to any release),
3. falls back to cargo install --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git callisto-cli (which hits the yanked bisync dependency on main).

It never runs cargo install callisto-cli against the published crates.io package, which is the one place that's actually known-good. That's the bug — in orin-dx/callisto's setup-callisto action, not in michi.

Fix: change that fallback branch (and ideally make it the primary path, ahead of the git-source fallback) to cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/.." --quiet pulling from crates.io. Since you maintain orin-dx/callisto too, want me to make that change there and open a PR?

✻ Churned for 35s · done 2:25 PM

❯ Oh, so what you're saying is that callisto's binary is not published so we fail

Right — two separate gaps, both in orin-dx/callisto:

1. No GitHub Release binary assets exist. Releases are cut (tags like callisto-cli@0.5.0) but nothing ever attaches callisto-macos-aarch64.tar.gz / callisto-linux-amd64.tar.gz etc. to them. So step 2 of the action (download prebuilt binary) always misses.
2. The git-source fallback is broken, separately, by the yanked bisync dep on main.

The action falls through both failing paths and never tries the one thing that would work: cargo install callisto-cli from crates.io, where 0.5.0 is already published and installable. That's the actual bug — the setup action doesn't know callisto ships via crates.io, so it fails even though a good install path exists.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(action): add crates.io fallback to setup-callisto's binary install

Production incident (2026-08-27, orin-dx/michi CI): setup-callisto's
install chain never tried crates.io. Step 1 (local monorepo build)
only applies inside this repo. Step 2 (GitHub Release binary tarball)
always 404s -- no release has ever had assets attached (that's the
separate, larger SPEC-007 feature). Step 3 (cargo install --git) was
separately broken on main by an unrelated yanked dependency. Every
external consumer fell through all three and failed, even though
callisto-cli@0.5.0 was already published and installable from
crates.io the whole time.

Adds a crates.io install attempt (cargo install callisto-cli --locked)
ahead of the git-source fallback, using the requested version (an
explicit "callisto-cli@X.Y.Z" tag strips to the bare semver crates.io
expects) or crates.io's own latest when unspecified. The git-source
fallback is kept as the final resort, not removed.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Nhu1NHHoF9pxzT8FVGobTJ
EOF
)"
git log --oneline -1
[/external_agent_tool_call]

## Summary
- **Production incident**: `setup-callisto`'s install chain never tried crates.io. External consumer CI (`orin-dx/michi`) fails because step 2 (GitHub Release binary tarball) always 404s -- no release has ever had assets attached (the separate, larger SPEC-007 feature covers that) -- and step 3 (`cargo install --git`) is separately broken on `main` by an unrelated yanked dependency. `callisto-cli@0.5.0` was already published and installable from crates.io the entire time; nothing tried it.

Here's a self-contained prompt — paste this to agy:

---

I need help closing out `.claude/specs/SPEC-007-github-release-binary-assets.json` in `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto` (repo root). This spec makes `publish-to = ["github-release"]` a working publish target: a package declares its own per-platform binary artifacts in `callisto.toml`, and `callisto publish` attaches them to the package's GitHub Release via `gh release upload`. It's already been through 3 rounds of `canon:exit-gate` review and failed each time (retry-count hit the escalation threshold, so it needs human/second-opinion input now rather than another automated retry).

Read the spec file fresh from disk first. It's in good shape overall — three prior rounds of fixes are already verified correct against live code. Three blockers remain from round 3:

**1. Design decision needed — `artifact_path` has no path-traversal validation.** The spec's `api_surface` claims `artifact_path` is "workspace-root-relative," but no acceptance criterion enforces that and no non-goal waives it. `parse_github_release_assets` (new function, `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs`) only errors on a missing/empty field — not on an absolute path or one containing `..`. Every other user-authored config path in this codebase (`[changesets].dir`, `[[package]] changelog`) is routed through `callisto_model::path::workspace_relative` (`crates/callisto-model/src/path.rs:25`), which rejects absolute paths and normalizes `..`. Without the same treatment here, a config like `path = "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key"` or `path = "../../secrets.pem"` would get uploaded as a public GitHub Release asset as-is, since the action.yml asset-attach loop just does `[[ -f "$ASSET_PATH" ]]` then `gh release upload`. **Decide:** validate `artifact_path` through `workspace_relative` (or an equivalent dedicated check) and add an `is_error_case: true` acceptance criterion for it, OR add an explicit non-goal stating this is deliberately unvalidated (and then the `api_surface`'s "workspace-root-relative" claim needs to be deleted or reworded, since it'd no longer be enforced). Recommend one and either make the edit or tell me which to make.

**2. Missing acceptance criteria — `[[package-set]]` asset declarations.** The spec's `scope` requires `github-release-assets` to resolve through "the same per-package-rule resolution (packages/package_sets, prefixed-then-bare matching)" that `publish_to` already uses, and the `RawGitHubReleaseAsset` api_surface entry requires `RawPackageSetConfig` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs:96`) to gain the field too — but every acceptance criterion (AC-001 etc.) only exercises `[[package]]`, never `[[package-set]]`. The parse-and-rewrap logic lives in two separate blocks inside `pub fn load` (`resolve.rs:231`): the `[[package]]` site at `resolve.rs:387-403` and the `[[package-set]]` site at `resolve.rs:457-473`. As written, an implementer could wire only the `[[package]]` site and every criterion would still pass. Add a criterion mirroring AC-001 but for a `[[package-set]]` block, plus one covering prefixed-over-bare precedence when both a `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]` rule declare `github-release-assets` for the same package.

**3. Mechanical fixes — wrong citations in `api_surface`.** The `parse_github_release_assets` entry says its error gets rewrapped by "`resolve_package_config`'s caller... (resolve.rs:167-171)" — both parts are wrong. `resolve.rs:167-171` is actually inside `parse_publish_target` itself (the error producer, not a rewrapper), and `resolve_package_config` is a pure rule-lookup function with no such caller relationship. The real rewrap happens in `load` (`resolve.rs:231`) at `resolve.rs:397-403` (`[[package]]`) and `resolve.rs:467-473` (`[[package-set]]`) — fix the citation to name both sites and their respective `"[[package]] github-release-assets: {key}"` / `"[[package-set]] github-release-assets: {key}"` prefixes. Also: scope item (5)'s `docs/01-spec.md` citation says lines 1740-1763 for the `ReleaseEntry` struct doc block, but it actually runs 1740-1770 (struct opens at 1742, closes at 1770) — fix to 1740-1770.

Once you've made a call on #1 and applied all three fixes directly to the spec JSON, re-run `canon:exit-gate` against it (or if you don't have that agent, just do a careful manual pass checking every acceptance criterion is testable, no TBDs, and the fixes are internally consistent) and let me know the verdict.

Not struggling — the 3 rounds of exit-gate review were adversarial by design, and each one caught real bugs (wrong field decomposition, an undefined type, a missing precondition, missing test coverage, wrong doc citations). That's the process working, not me failing. And I'd hold off calling agy's pass fully correct — I just found something in a 5-minute check.

Agy's fix reuses `ConfigError::UnknownKey` for the path-validation error. But I checked the actual precedent it claims to match: `changelog` and `changesets.dir` — the two existing fields that already validate through `workspace_relative` — both use **dedicated error variants** (`ConfigError::InvalidChangelogPath`, `ConfigError::InvalidChangesetsDir`), not `UnknownKey`:

```
crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:374
callisto_model::workspace_relative(s).map_err(|_err| ConfigError::InvalidChangelogPath { ... })
```

`UnknownKey` is what this codebase uses for a missing/malformed key — reusing it for "this key is present but its path shape is invalid" is a real inconsistency with the pattern agy's own spec says it's matching. (One thing agy got right that I want to be fair about: the `callisto_model::workspace_relative` path itself is correct — it's re-exported at the crate root via `pub use path::*;`, so no citation bug there.)

Fix is small — one paragraph in `api_surface` plus AC-018 need to say `ConfigError::InvalidGitHubReleaseAssetPath` (or similar dedicated variant) instead of `UnknownKey`. Want me to make that edit directly, or send it back to agy?

payload.message:
Two more, one of them substantive:

**2. AC-020's precedence description is wrong.** It says `[[package]]` beats `[[package-set]]` "following standard prefixed-then-bare package rule precedence" — but that's not the real mechanism. I traced it in `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:340-360`:
- "Prefixed-then-bare" is a *different, unrelated* precedence axis — it only governs ordering *within* `[[package]]` rules themselves (ecosystem-prefixed rules beat bare-name rules, both still `[[package]]`).
- `[[package]]` vs `[[package-set]]` is a **separate mechanism entirely**: `let active_override = pkg_override.or(set_override);` — if any `[[package]]` rule matches at all, the *whole* `[[package-set]]`'s config is discarded for that package, not merged field-by-field. So if a `[[package]]` rule matches but doesn't itself declare `github-release-assets`, AC-020's scenario doesn't even apply the way it's written — the package-set's assets are shadowed regardless, by whole-object override, not by "precedence" between two field values. Real behavior, correctly directionally right, but the spec's explanation of *why* is factually wrong and would mislead whoever implements it.

**3. Minor: acceptance-criteria numbering is out of order** — AC-017 sits between AC-008 and AC-009 (agy inserted it there instead of appending after AC-016/AC-018-020). Purely cosmetic, doesn't affect correctness, but worth a quick renumber for readability before this ships.

So: 1 real design-consistency bug (error variant), 1 real factual inaccuracy in a criterion's mechanism description (could mislead implementation), 1 cosmetic issue. Want me to fix all three directly in the spec now?

payload.message:
Something else for you to look into and deliberate:

Short answer on the four tools: none of them solve this natively. They're all version-bump/changelog engines; the native-binary-publish-ordering problem is universally solved by bolting napi-rs's own tooling (napi build / napi create-npm-dirs / napi artifacts / napi prepublish) onto a custom CI step, regardless of which one you use.

- Changesets: platform packages are typically listed in .changeset/config.json's ignore array — excluded from changesets' own version-bump/changelog reasoning entirely. A separate build-matrix CI step generates each platform package.json (version copied from the main package, not independently decided) and npm publishs it directly. Changesets only ever publishes the wrapper package, after that matrix step finishes.
- release-please: same shape — its manifest config only tracks "real" packages; platform dirs are generated/published by a hand-rolled matrix job release-please knows nothing about.
- Nx release: closest to first-class support, because Nx itself ships this way. It models the platform packages as real projects in the dependency graph, so nx release publish respects topological order (native packages before the wrapper) automatically. The binary build + optionalDependencies injection is still custom, but the ordering is a built-in primitive there in a way it isn't in the others.
- Knope: lower confidence, but I'm not aware of it having anything special here either — same custom-matrix pattern would apply.

The common thread: version-bump tools treat these platform packages as either invisible or as dumb publish targets whose version is copied, never independently decided. The actual "build N binaries, publish each first, then publish the thing that depends on them" choreography always lives in your own CI, not the release tool.

For your repo specifically, I checked callisto.toml — it's worse than "not sequenced," it's not tracked at all. The [[package]] list only covers 2 crates + 3 npm wrapper packages (cli, napi, vite-plugin). All 10 platform packages (5 for cli, 5 for napi) have zero entry in callisto's publish plan. So right now, even a working callisto run would never publish them — this isn't just an ordering gap, it's a missing step entirely.

Recommendation: yes, wire it into release.yml, structured as three phases:
1. Callisto does version-decision only (no publish) — it needs to run first regardless, since the platform packages' versions are copied from whatever it decides for cli/napi.
2. A new build-matrix job (per target) runs napi b/manual package.json generation with the now-knownversion → npm publish for each of the 10 platform packages, keyed off Cargo's oxc-react-docgen/oxc-react-docgen-napi versionthat callisto just decided.
3. Callisto's actual publish: true step runs last, publishing cli/napi/vite-plugin — by which point their optionalDependencies resolve cleanly.

That's a real workflow restructure (splitting call publish calls, adding a build matrix), not a small patch. Want me to check whether callisto-action/the callisto CLI even exposes a version-only vs. publish-only split before I sketch the actual release.yml changes?

Dug into this rather than just accept the recommendation — found something that changes it.

**The tool-comparison analysis (changesets/release-please/nx/knope) reads as solid and consistent with known napi-rs monorepo patterns** — I can't independently verify those other repos' exact configs from here, but nothing in it looks wrong.

**The callisto-specific analysis and recommendation need a correction, though.** I checked `PublishOrchestrator::execute` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:679`) directly:

```rust
for rust_crate in &plan.rust_crates { ... }
for npm_pkg in &plan.npm_platform_packages { ... }   // <- platform packages
for npm_pkg in &plan.npm_main_packages { ... }        // <- wrapper package, published AFTER
for pypi_pkg in &plan.pypi_packages { ... }
```

**Callisto already publishes native platform packages before the main/wrapper package, unconditionally, by category.** Combined with SPEC-006 (native artifact placement into package dirs before publish — shipped this session) and fixed-group version alignment (platform + wrapper packages share one version via `callisto.toml` groups), callisto's existing machinery already does most of the 3-phase choreography agy is proposing to hand-build: version decision → artifact placement → ordered publish (platform first) is already how `callisto publish` works internally, in one pass.

So the real question for that repo isn't "does callisto support this ordering" — it does. It's: **are the 10 platform packages actually configured as discoverable workspace members in the right fixed group**, with `napi.targets` correctly declared so `walk.rs` classifies them as `npm_platform_packages` in the first place? If not, that's a `callisto.toml`/manifest-configuration gap in that repo, not a missing callisto feature — and the fix is much smaller than a custom CI build-matrix-plus-3-phase-workflow rewrite (still need the CI job that *builds* the N native binaries, that's unavoidable and outside callisto's job — but the placement/versioning/publish-ordering choreography around them is already callisto's job).

One more thing worth their attention: `depends_on_platforms: Vec<String>` (`crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:106`) is populated at construction but I found zero consumers reading it for ordering logic — the category-based loop above ignores it entirely. It's either dead weight or meant for something not yet wired up. Worth asking them to check before assuming it does anything.

command: cd /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto
gh pr create --title "fix(graph): skip publishing an npm main package when a declared platform dependency fails" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- `PublishOrchestrator::execute` computed `depends_on_platforms` correctly (from the real dependency graph, in `plan_publish`) but never consulted it during publish -- a main/wrapper npm package would still be published even if a platform package it optionally depends on just failed in the same run, shipping `optionalDependencies` referencing a version that was never actually uploaded.
- Fixed: before attempting to publish an `npm_main_packages` entry, check whether any of its `depends_on_platforms` failed earlier in the same run; if so, skip the actual publish attempt (never calls the registry client) and record it as a `Failed { kind: "dependencyFailed", .. }` attempt naming the failed dependency, so it's visible in the report rather than silently missing.

## Why
Found while reviewing a downstream napi-rs monorepo's publish-ordering question. The existing category-based publish order (all platform packages attempted before any main package) already prevents most of this class of problem, but doesn't prevent a wrapper from publishing anyway when one of its *specific* declared platform dependencies genuinely failed.

## Test Plan
- [x] New `npm_main_package_is_skipped_when_its_platform_dependency_fails` test -- confirmed RED before the fix (main package got `Published` despite its platform dep failing), GREEN after
- [x] Full `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib` -- 412 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` -- clean
EOF
)" --label bug --base main --head fix-publish-order-platform-dependency-gating 2>&1
[/external_agent_tool_call]

payload.message:
From agy:

  Here is a comprehensive code review of PR #23: fix(graph): skip publishing an npm main package when a declared platform     
  dependency fails https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/23 across correctness, architecture, performance, and DX.         
  ──────                                                                                                                      
  ### 1. Correctness & Bug: Cross-Ecosystem False-Positive Collision                                                          
                                                                                                                              
  #### The Defect                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                              
  In publish.rs:705-709:                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                              
    let failed_platform_names: std::collections::HashSet<String> = attempts                                                   
        .iter()                                                                                                               
        .filter(|a| a.result.is_failure())                                                                                    
        .map(|a| a.package.name().to_string())                                                                                
        .collect();                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                              
  Prior to line 705, attempts contains published and failed attempts from both plan.rust_crates (Cargo) and                   
  plan.npm_platform_packages (npm).                                                                                           
                                                                                                                              
  Because .map(|a| a.package.name().to_string()) strips the ecosystem prefix (Ecosystem::Cargo vs Ecosystem::Npm), if a Cargo 
  crate publish to crates.io fails (e.g. network glitch, auth/token issue, or crates.io rate limiting) on a crate named my-   
  cli-linux-x64 (or core, native, plugin), its bare name is collected into failed_platform_names.                             
                                                                                                                              
  When the npm_main_packages loop subsequently executes:                                                                      
                                                                                                                              
    let failed_deps: Vec<&str> = npm_pkg                                                                                      
        .depends_on_platforms                                                                                                 
        .iter()                                                                                                               
        .map(String::as_str)                                                                                                  
        .filter(|dep| failed_platform_names.contains(*dep))                                                                   
        .collect();

payload.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This is a very long, multi-phase session on the `callisto` repo (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto`), a Rust-based monorepo release-automation tool comparable to changesets/knope/release-please/Nx release. The session covered many sequential user-driven tasks:
   - Continue closing `callisto-cli` crate coverage to 90% (pre-existing work), open PR for SPEC-006 (native CI artifact placement).
   - After merging PR #15 (SPEC-006) and PR #16 (auto release), user asked to check the release PR was correct, then to keep tackling issues found (probe_git wiring → PR #17; a floating major-version git-tag force-push bug → PR #18; closing out the 2026-08-12 workspace audit as fully resolved → PR #19).
   - User asked to resolve merge conflicts and rebase PR #18 and #19 onto latest main (done, both merged).
   - User asked to fix the stale floating tags on the real remote (force-push repair, explicitly approved) → PR #21 (doc closure).
   - User asked "feature-wise are we completely done???" and "So we have ALL of the core changeset, knope, release please, nx release features??? Anything missing?" — led to real research (WebSearch-backed fork) comparing callisto against changesets/knope/release-please/Nx release.
   - User asked "Do we have the ability to release binaries to GH releases?" — confirmed NO (PublishTarget::GitHubRelease is an explicitly-unimplemented stub).
   - User said "Let's tackle github release" — kicked off the full canon→vector pipeline (graph:intake → graph:clarifier → canon:drafter → canon:auditor → canon:exit-gate ×3 rounds → vector:planner) for a new SPEC-007 feature (GitHub Release binary asset uploads), general-purpose scope per explicit user answer to an AskUserQuestion.
   - Mid-stream, user reported a real production incident: "All users of callisto are failing because we don't have a published binary to GH, we need to get this done quickly please" — investigated, found this was actually about `setup-callisto` action's install fallback never trying crates.io (a separate, faster fix from SPEC-007) → PR #22 (hotfix), with a real regression test.
   - User then relayed messages from a separate agent named "agy" (working on a different repo, `oxc-react-docgen`, but reviewing callisto's own SPEC-007 spec and later PR #23) — user acted as relay, asking me to independently verify agy's claims each round rather than trust them, per repeated explicit instruction: "shall I have agy take a look?" → user asked me to draft a handoff prompt for agy → agy did 2 rounds of spec-fixing (both independently verified by me, found real remaining issues each time, which agy then fixed correctly in round 2).
   - User asked me to deliberate on a different agy message about napi-rs monorepo publish-ordering patterns (for a different repo), leading me to discover and confirm a real bug in callisto itself: `NpmMainPublish.depends_on_platforms` was computed but never consulted during publish.
   - User said "if we have bugs fix it" — TDD fix implemented → PR #23.
   - User asked "Are you fully confident on the work done?" — I gave a calibrated, non-blanket answer, and verified one previously-unverified risk (`cargo install --locked` requires the crate to include `Cargo.lock`; confirmed via `cargo package --list` that `callisto-cli` does include it).
   - User relayed a code review from agy on PR #23 identifying a real cross-ecosystem name-collision bug in my fix (a failed Cargo crate could be mistaken for a failed npm platform dependency because `.name()` strips ecosystem). I independently verified this was real, and also caught that agy's suggested patch (reverting to `HashSet<&str>` borrowing from `attempts`) would not compile due to the exact borrow-checker conflict (E0502) I had already fixed earlier by switching to owned `String`s — despite agy's claim "All tests in callisto-graph passed (412 tests)". I fixed this correctly via TDD (RED test proving the collision, confirmed RED, then fixed by adding `a.package.ecosystem() == Some(Ecosystem::Npm)` to the filter, keeping owned `String`s).
   - Most recent message: user asked to run a comprehensive adversarial investigation (bugs, perf, corner/error cases, DX, security) "Use agent teams wih the most appropriate model and effort in a comprehensive workflow" — but this message came bundled with an automated system instruction demanding a text-only, no-tool-call summary response (this exact compaction). The adversarial investigation itself has NOT been started.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Rust workspace: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; crates `callisto-model`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto-cli`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-format`, `callisto-changelog`, `callisto-conventional`, `callisto-vcs`, `callisto-moon`, `callisto-fixtures` (10 total; `callisto-fixtures` has `publish = false`, dev-only, AGPL, correctly never tagged/released).
   - `just`-only CI/dev-workflow discipline (never raw `cargo`/`moon` in GH Actions YAML); `just ci-fast` default; `just coverage [threshold]` / `just coverage-per-crate [threshold]`.
   - canon→vector→lambda spec-driven pipeline (agents: `graph:intake`, `graph:clarifier`, `canon:drafter`, `canon:auditor`, `canon:exit-gate`, `vector:planner`, `vector:challenger`, `lambda:*`) — used extensively for SPEC-007. Correct agent names confirmed via trial/error (NOT `canon:draft-spec`/`canon:audit-spec`/`graph:clarify-requirement` — those don't exist; correct ones are `canon:drafter`, `canon:auditor`, `graph:clarifier`).
   - Fork/Agent/SendMessage tool distinction: resuming a background agent MUST use `SendMessage({to: agentId, ...})`, NOT `Agent` tool with a `to` param (which silently spawns a fresh, context-less agent) — this mistake was made twice this session (once with `af0cfa606a931b28d`, once with `ab5b6a14e88ee98c3`/`ac07cd3774477b160`), each time caught and cleaned up via `TaskStop`.
   - Stale/mid-flight agent result recognition: a `status: completed` notification with a placeholder-shaped `result` (e.g. "Waiting for X to return...") must be treated as NOT actually done — resume via `SendMessage`, don't trust the placeholder.
   - `PublishOrchestrator::execute` (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs) publishes in fixed category order: `rust_crates` → `npm_platform_packages` → `npm_main_packages` → `pypi_packages`, per-package independent (no abort-on-first-failure), each result recorded as `PublishAttempt`.
   - `NpmMainPublish.depends_on_platforms: Vec<String>` — computed correctly in `plan_publish` (walks `ws.graph.dependencies_of(&pkg.id)`, filters edges to packages with `ManifestRole::Platform`, collects `.name()`) but was never consulted at publish time until this session's fix.
   - `PackageId::ecosystem() -> Option<Ecosystem>` (crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:94) and `PackageId::name() -> &str` — `.name()` alone is ecosystem-unaware; comparing bare names across ecosystems is an unsafe pattern ("Raw String Identity Smell").
   - GitHub Release / floating major-version tags: `callisto tag --floating-major` correctly force-moves the LOCAL tag ref (`git tag -f`), but `callisto-action`'s `git push origin --tags` (no `--force`) can never move an already-existing REMOTE tag — root cause of PR #18. Operator machine's global `tag.gpgSign=true` forces annotated+signed tags even for plain `git tag <name> <commit>`, causing "fatal: no tag message?" — must override locally via `git -c tag.gpgSign=false tag -f ...` for one-off manual ops, without touching the real gitconfig.
   - `setup-callisto/action.yml`'s binary-install fallback chain: (1) local monorepo build, (2) GitHub Release binary tarball download (currently always 404s — no release ever had assets attached, that's SPEC-007's whole purpose), (3) `cargo install --git ...` (was broken on `main` by an unrelated yanked `bisync` dependency, per relayed agy diagnosis) — fixed by adding a crates.io install attempt (`cargo install callisto-cli --locked` or `--version X.Y.Z --locked`) ahead of the git-source fallback.
   - `cargo install --locked` requires the published crate to include `Cargo.lock` — verified true for `callisto-cli` via `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` (binary crates get Cargo.lock auto-included by cargo since 1.37+, confirmed empirically here, not just from memory, since network access to crates.io was unavailable in this sandbox).
   - `RegistryError` variants: `RateLimited(Duration)`, `AuthFailed(String)`, `Network(String)`, `Other(String)`; `.kind_str()` gives camelCase discriminators ("rateLimited", "authFailed", "network", "other"). New ad-hoc kind `"dependencyFailed"` introduced (constructed directly in the orchestrator, not from `RegistryError`, so no new `RegistryError` variant needed).
   - `PublishAttemptResult::Failed { kind: String, error: String }`, `.is_failure()`; `PublishReport::has_failures()`.
   - Borrow-checker constraint discovered and fixed twice this session: `HashSet<&str>` borrowed from `attempts` conflicts with later `attempts.push(...)` in the same scope (E0502) — must use owned `String`s (`HashSet<String>`) instead, or scope the borrow tightly. This is the exact issue in agy's rejected "zero-allocation" suggestion.
   - `workspace_relative()` (crates/callisto-model/src/path.rs:25, re-exported as `callisto_model::workspace_relative` via `pub use path::*;` in lib.rs) — rejects absolute paths (`ModelError::AbsolutePath`), normalizes `.`/`..` lexically, returns `Result<PathBuf, ModelError>` (NOT `ConfigError` directly — needs explicit `.map_err`). Established codebase precedent: dedicated `ConfigError` variants per validated-path field (`InvalidChangesetsDir` E116, `InvalidChangelogPath` E113), NOT reuse of `ConfigError::UnknownKey`. SPEC-007's `ConfigError::InvalidGitHubReleaseAssetPath` (E121, confirmed next-free code, no collision) follows this precedent correctly after agy's round-2 fix.
   - `[[package]]` vs `[[package-set]]` precedence: NOT "prefixed-then-bare" (that's a different axis, entirely within `[[package]]` rules via `resolve_package_config`'s two-pass search in crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:199-219). Real mechanism: `let active_override = pkg_override.or(set_override);` in crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:340-360 — a WHOLE-OBJECT override (if any `[[package]]` rule matches at all, the entire `[[package-set]]` config is discarded for that package, not merged field-by-field). This was a real factual error agy's spec initially had (AC-020) and correctly fixed in round 2.
   - napi-rs monorepo publish patterns: changesets/release-please treat platform packages as invisible/dumb publish targets (custom hand-rolled CI matrix); Nx release has first-class dependency-graph-aware ordering. Callisto's own `PublishOrchestrator::execute` already does category-based ordering (platform packages before main packages) — closer to Nx's approach than initially assumed by a relayed external analysis, though the `depends_on_platforms` field itself was unused until this session's fix.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs` — THE actively-edited file for the final bugfix (PR #23). Current state after both fix rounds:
     ```rust
     pub fn execute(&self, plan: &PublishPlan, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> PublishReport {
         let mut attempts = Vec::new();
         for rust_crate in &plan.rust_crates { /* unchanged */ }
         for npm_pkg in &plan.npm_platform_packages { /* unchanged */ }

         // Names of npm platform packages that did NOT successfully publish
         // above (Published/AlreadyPublished both count as success). ...
         // Scoped to `Ecosystem::Npm`: `depends_on_platforms` is an npm-only
         // construct, and a bare `.name()` carries no ecosystem information,
         // so an unscoped comparison could mistake a same-named failed Cargo
         // crate for a failed npm platform dependency.
         let failed_platform_names: std::collections::HashSet<String> = attempts
             .iter()
             .filter(|a| a.package.ecosystem() == Some(Ecosystem::Npm) && a.result.is_failure())
             .map(|a| a.package.name().to_string())
             .collect();

         for npm_pkg in &plan.npm_main_packages {
             let pkg_id = PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem: Ecosystem::Npm, name: npm_pkg.name.clone() };
             let failed_deps: Vec<&str> = npm_pkg.depends_on_platforms.iter()
                 .map(String::as_str)
                 .filter(|dep| failed_platform_names.contains(*dep))
                 .collect();
             if !failed_deps.is_empty() {
                 attempts.push(PublishAttempt {
                     package: pkg_id,
                     version: npm_pkg.version.clone(),
                     result: PublishAttemptResult::Failed {
                         kind: "dependencyFailed".to_string(),
                         error: format!(
                             "skipped: platform dependenc{} failed to publish: {}",
                             if failed_deps.len() == 1 { "y" } else { "ies" },
                             failed_deps.join(", ")
                         ),
                     },
                 });
                 continue;
             }
             self.emit_progress(&npm_pkg.name, &npm_pkg.version);
             attempts.push(self.attempt_publish(pkg_id, npm_pkg.version.clone(), permit));
         }
         for pypi_pkg in &plan.pypi_packages { /* unchanged */ }
         PublishReport { schema_version: callisto_model::SCHEMA_VERSION, attempts, diagnostics: Vec::new() }
     }
     ```
     Two new tests added to the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block:
     - `npm_main_package_is_skipped_when_its_platform_dependency_fails` (original bug's regression test; committed in PR #23's first commit `973406f6`).
     - `cargo_crate_failure_does_not_false_positive_match_an_npm_platform_dependency_of_the_same_name` (round-2 collision test; just written, confirmed RED against the pre-ecosystem-filter code, fix just applied, GREEN not yet independently re-confirmed post-fix — full-suite run `b77aukw6p` was in flight when compaction triggered).
   - `.github/actions/setup-callisto/action.yml` — modified in PR #22 (hotfix branch `hotfix-setup-callisto-crates-io-fallback`, merged separately from the graph fix branch). Added crates.io install attempts before the git-source fallback:
     ```bash
     CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto-cli@}"
     if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml" ]] && grep -q "callisto-cli" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml"; then
       # local build (unchanged)
     elif curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o /tmp/callisto.tar.gz 2>/dev/null; then
       # GH release download (unchanged)
     elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
       echo "Callisto installed from crates.io (latest)"
       cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
     elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --version "$CRATE_VERSION" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
       echo "Callisto installed from crates.io ($CRATE_VERSION)"
       cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
     else
       echo "Installing from git source (crates.io install failed or was skipped)..."
       cargo install --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git callisto-cli --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
       cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
     fi
     ```
   - `.github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh` — new test file (PR #22), extracts the action.yml snippet by explicit line-number range (comment-anchor to `CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> $GITHUB_PATH`), stubs `curl`/`cargo`, confirmed RED against pre-fix action.yml via `git stash`, GREEN after.
   - `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml` — modified in PR #18: `git push origin --tags || true` → `git push origin --tags --force` (no more silent swallow).
   - `.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_tag_push_force.sh` — new regression test for PR #18.
   - `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md` — updated multiple times with terse, UNWRAPPED (per explicit user instruction "DO NOT WRAP ANY OF OUR MARKDOWN!!!!!") entries for: SPEC-006 (merged), probe_git fix, floating-tag fix + its follow-up closure, 2026-08-12 audit closure summary.
   - `/Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/memory/project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md` and `MEMORY.md` — updated to record the audit as fully CLOSED (31/31 medium/low findings re-verified fixed via a 31-agent parallel workflow, cross-checked by hand on 4 of them).
   - `.claude/specs/SPEC-007-github-release-binary-assets.json` — new spec file, went through 2 full rounds of independent adversarial review (mine via `canon:exit-gate` ×3 automated rounds hitting retry-escalation, then me + agy manually, 2 more rounds). Final state (post agy round 2, independently verified by me as fully correct): 20 acceptance criteria (AC-001–AC-020, sequential), `api_surface` includes `GitHubReleaseAsset`, `ReleaseEntry.assets`, `PackageConfig.github_release_assets`, `RawGitHubReleaseAsset`, `ConfigError::InvalidGitHubReleaseAssetPath` (E121), `parse_github_release_assets`, `GraphError::MissingGitHubReleaseAssets`, the action.yml asset-attach loop. Confirmed NOT yet implemented (spec+plan only).
   - `.claude/plans/PLAN-007.json` — new plan file from `vector:planner`, 12 tasks (`MODEL-1..3`, `GRAPH-1..6`, `ACTION-1`, `CLI-1`, `DOC-1`) across 5 batches, all 20 ACs covered, `spec_hash: sha256:c99dbc7a486ec0f0b7ca31ccfc7060c54de28df7effd39755864d162ac83940a`.    - `RegistryError` variants: `RateLimited(Duration)`, `AuthFailed(String)`, `Network(String)`, `Other(String)`; `.kind_str()` gives camelCase discriminators ("rateLimited", "authFailed", "network", "other"). New ad-hoc kind `"dependencyFailed"` introduced (constructed directly in the orchestrator, not from `RegistryError`, so no new `RegistryError` variant needed).
   - `PublishAttemptResult::Failed { kind: String, error: String }`, `.is_failure()`; `PublishReport::has_failures()`.

This is the exact issue in agy's rejected "zero-allocation" suggestion.
   - `workspace_relative()` (crates/callisto-model/src/path.rs:25, re-exported as `callisto_model::workspace_relative` via `pub use path::*;` in lib.rs) — rejects absolute paths (`ModelError::AbsolutePath`), normalizes `.`/`..` lexically, returns `Result<PathBuf, ModelError>` (NOT `ConfigError` directly — needs explicit `.map_err`). Established codebase precedent: dedicated `ConfigError` variants per validated-path field (`InvalidChangesetsDir` E116, `InvalidChangelogPath` E113), NOT reuse of `ConfigError::UnknownKey`. SPEC-007's `ConfigError::InvalidGitHubReleaseAssetPath` (E121, confirmed next-free code, no collision) follows this precedent correctly after agy's round-2 fix.

Real mechanism: `let active_override = pkg_override.or(set_override);` in crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:340-360 — a WHOLE-OBJECT override (if any `[[package]]` rule matches at all, the entire `[[package-set]]` config is discarded for that package, not merged field-by-field). This was a real factual error agy's spec initially had (AC-020) and correctly fixed in round 2.
   - napi-rs monorepo publish patterns: changesets/release-please treat platform packages as invisible/dumb publish targets (custom hand-rolled CI matrix); Nx release has first-class dependency-graph-aware ordering. Callisto's own `PublishOrchestrator::execute` already does category-based ordering (platform packages before main packages) — closer to Nx's approach than initially assumed by a relayed external analysis, though the `depends_on_platforms` field itself was unused until this session's fix.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs` — THE actively-edited file for the final bugfix (PR #23). Current state after both fix rounds:
     ```rust
     pub fn execute(&self, plan: &PublishPlan, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> PublishReport {
         let mut attempts = Vec::new();
         for rust_crate in &plan.rust_crates { /* unchanged */ }
         for npm_pkg in &plan.npm_platform_packages { /* unchanged */ }

         // Names of npm platform packages that did NOT successfully publish
         // above (Published/AlreadyPublished both count as success). ...
         // Scoped to `Ecosystem::Npm`: `depends_on_platforms` is an npm-only
         // construct, and a bare `.name()` carries no ecosystem information,
         // so an unscoped comparison could mistake a same-named failed Cargo
         // crate for a failed npm platform dependency.
         let failed_platform_names: std::collections::HashSet<String> = attempts
             .iter()
             .filter(|a| a.package.ecosystem() == Some(Ecosystem::Npm) && a.result.is_failure())
             .map(|a| a.package.name().to_string())
             .collect();

         for npm_pkg in &plan.npm_main_packages {
             let pkg_id = PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem: Ecosystem::Npm, name: npm_pkg.name.clone() };
             let failed_deps: Vec<&str> = npm_pkg.depends_on_platforms.iter()
                 .map(String::as_str)
                 .filter(|dep| failed_platform_names.contains(*dep))
                 .collect();
             if !failed_deps.is_empty() {
                 attempts.push(PublishAttempt {
                     package: pkg_id,
                     version: npm_pkg.version.clone(),
                     result: PublishAttemptResult::Failed {
                         kind: "dependencyFailed".to_string(),
                         error: format!(
                             "skipped: platform dependenc{} failed to publish: {}",
                             if failed_deps.len() == 1 { "y" } else { "ies" },
                             failed_deps.join(", ")
                         ),
                     },
                 });
                 continue;
             }
             self.emit_progress(&npm_pkg.name, &npm_pkg.version);
             attempts.push(self.attempt_publish(pkg_id, npm_pkg.version.clone(), permit));
         }
         for pypi_pkg in &plan.pypi_packages { /* unchanged */ }
         PublishReport { schema_version: callisto_model::SCHEMA_VERSION, attempts, diagnostics: Vec::new() }

I have the full findings list (18 confirmed, 2 refuted). No need to read the rest — the JSON result already gave complete detail. Here's the report.

## Adversarial audit: publish pipeline — 18 confirmed findings

Scoped to `publish.rs`, `publish_client.rs`, and the two Action scripts (`setup-callisto`, `callisto-action`). 46 agents, 2 skeptics per finding, 2 refuted and dropped.

**Critical (2)**
1. **`git push origin --tags --force` clobbers immutable release tags**, not just the floating-major alias (`callisto-action/action.yml:208-211`) — the composite action creates real per-version tags without `-f` (correctly relying on git's non-fast-forward protection), then blanket force-pushes *all* local tags. Any divergence silently overwrites a historical release tag with no error, instead of git rejecting it.
2. **`depends_on_platforms` is never validated against what's actually in the plan** — a misconfigured or `--package`-filtered-out platform package produces zero diagnostics; the main npm package ships referencing an `optionalDependencies` version that was never published.

**High (7)** — Dev-edge fallback in `publish_order` silently drops dev-ordering for the *entire* plan (not just the cyclic pair) once any dev cycle exists anywhere; `plan-publish` computed twice per release (no way to hand the already-computed JSON to `callisto publish`); empty plan reported as `published=true`; one package's publish failure aborts the whole step before tagging/releasing already-succeeded siblings; `--package` filter doesn't cascade to `depends_on_platforms`, letting a main package publish against a dependency that was filtered out of the run; `UnknownPackage` error text is misleading for two of its three real trigger causes; live stderr streaming in CI logs bypasses the credential-redaction that the final error string gets — real registry tokens can hit a public Actions log; unescaped `${{ inputs.version }}` interpolated into raw bash in `setup-callisto` is a script-injection primitive for any external caller; `cargo install --git` fallback ignores the requested version/tag entirely and has no integrity check, trusting upstream HEAD with live publish credentials.

**Medium (3)** — `--package`/`only` filter matches bare names across ecosystems (a Cargo crate and npm package sharing a name both get swept in); redundant `npm view` pre-check subprocess before every npm publish that buys nothing over the existing conflict-classification; `docs/06-publishing.md` documents nothing about the platform/main split or `dependencyFailed`.

**Low (2)** — Windows fallback download saves a `.zip` as `.tar.gz` and extracts with `tar -xzf` (always fails on Windows outside the monorepo); GitHub Release loop spawns 3 `jq` processes per entry instead of 1.

Full detail (exact scenarios, line numbers, suggested fixes) is in the task output. Want me to start fixing these — and if so, in what order (I'd suggest the two criticals first, then the tag-push/force-push family together since they're the same root cause)?

## Triple-check + fix plan: publish pipeline

**64 agents, 3 independent skeptics per finding, then cluster → design → adversarial challenge.**

### Triple-check result: 15/18 survived a third round
Dropped: **F5** (double plan-compute), **F17** (unescaped `inputs.version` injection), **F18** (cargo-install fallback ignores version/no integrity check) — a third independent reader could not substantiate these as real/reachable. I'm treating them as not-confirmed rather than digging further; flag if you want a fourth opinion on any of the three.

### Important process finding (the challenge phase caught this by checking real git state, not just the designs)
The plan as clustered assumes "branch fresh off main," but that's false today:
- **`fix-publish-order-platform-dependency-gating`** (the branch we're on right now, 2 commits ahead of main) already implements half of cluster C4 — same function names, same test names the C4 design independently re-derived. This needs to merge to main **before** C4 starts, or C4 gets branched from here instead of main.
- **`hotfix-setup-callisto-crates-io-fallback`** (unmerged, 1 commit) already edits the exact lines F4 (Windows zip/tar.gz) targets. Needs reconciling before F4 starts.

Skipping this risks silently duplicating already-reviewed work — matches the "parallel-fixing anti-pattern" and "found code needs same rigor" lessons already in memory.

### Clusters and recommended order
1. **C4 — `F3+F11+F12+F13`** (package-filter/`depends_on_platforms` semantic integrity, `publish.rs`). Reuses existing `PackageId::matches`/`resolve_target_package` machinery; adds two new `GraphError` variants (E121/E122, confirmed free); no schema/wire changes. **Land first** — most invasive, everything else in this file shifts around it.
2. **C3 — `F2`** (Dev-cycle fallback drops ordering plan-wide). SCC-scoped exclusion instead of a global kind-list retry; algorithmically isolated (only production caller of `toposort_impl`). Challenge phase found a real gap: no test for a *mixed* Runtime+Dev cyclic pair — add one.
3. **C5 — `F6`** (redundant npm `is_published` pre-check). Made opt-in via `--skip-publish-precheck`, default behavior unchanged — safer than removing it outright, since removal would re-run npm lifecycle scripts on a retried publish.
4. **C1 — `F1+F8+F9+F10+F15`** (action.yml publish→tag→release block). The real fix: push "which packages actually published" and "which tags are floating vs. immutable" into Rust (`filter_plan_by_report`, `CreatedTag.is_floating_major`) instead of guessing in bash — this is what lets F1 (scope force-push) and F15 (stop swallowing errors) be fixed together safely. Has an undeclared soft dependency on C4 (needs the `dependencyFailed` attempt kind C4/the current branch defines). Challenge phase found two real gaps: no test for zero-floating or zero-immutable tag batches (bash empty-array footgun under `set -u`), and the artifact-placement guard test needs a `callisto` stub it doesn't have yet.
5. **C2 — `F7`** (native artifact loop: jq consolidation). Must land **after** C1 — confirmed same physical lines (168-179), guaranteed textual conflict otherwise. Deliberately does *not* parallelize `gh run download` — SPEC-006 AC-006 pins sequential fail-fast semantics.
6. **C6 — `F16`** (live stderr credential leak). File-isolated to `runner.rs`, no trait signature change. Verified sound with no gaps.
7. **C7 — `F4`** (Windows zip/tar.gz). File-isolated but blocked on reconciling the hotfix branch above first.
8. **C8 — `F14`** (docs). Last — must describe `depends_on_platforms`/`dependencyFailed` as C4 leaves them, not before.

### Not safe to run as 8 parallel worktrees
Four clusters (C1, C3, C4, C5) all touch `publish.rs` — no logical overlap, but they share a test-module tail and would collide as parallel branches. Correct execution is **serialized within each shared file, cluster-by-cluster, with validation after each** — matches your established preference already. C6 and C7 (once its hotfix conflict is resolved) are the only two safe to fully parallelize against everything else.

Want me to start with the git-state reconciliation (merge/rebase the two in-flight branches) and then C4, one cluster at a time with a green suite between each?

description: Commit cluster 1 fix
command: git add crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs crates/callisto-graph/tests/publish_tests.rs
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(graph): validate package filtering and platform dependencies against the real plan

Three related gaps in plan_publish, all sharing the same root cause:
nothing cross-checked what --package selected or what depends_on_platforms
declared against what actually ended up in the final plan.

- --only ("--package") matched by bare name only, so a Cargo crate and an
  npm package sharing a name (e.g. "core") were both silently swept into
  a filtered plan. Each requested name is now resolved to a single,
  disambiguated PackageId via PackageId::resolve_unique against the full
  workspace membership before any filtering happens; a genuine cross-
  ecosystem collision reuses the existing GraphError::AmbiguousName and
  tells the caller to qualify it (npm:core).

- An npm main package's depends_on_platforms was never checked against
  what actually shipped in the plan. A misconfigured platform sibling
  (no npm publish target) or one filtered out by --only would let the
  main package publish anyway, referencing an optionalDependencies
  version that was never uploaded. Now cross-checked after filtering,
  allowing through only a dependency that's either present in the plan
  or already published (its version already tag-matches). New error:
  GraphError::MissingPlatformDependency (E121).

- --package naming a real workspace package that simply had nothing to
  do (not a release candidate, or no dispatchable target) returned the
  same UnknownPackage message as a genuine typo, sending an operator to
  check workspace membership when that was never the problem. New error:
  GraphError::PackageNotInPublishPlan (E122), discriminating NotARelease
  from NoDispatchableTarget.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"
[/external_agent_tool_call]

[external_agent_tool_call: Bash]
description: Open PR for cluster 1
command: gh pr create --base fix-publish-order-platform-dependency-gating --head fix-package-filter-platform-dependency-validation --title "fix(graph): validate package filtering and platform dependencies against the real plan" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Stacked on #23 — depends on it merging first (this branch builds on the `depends_on_platforms`/`dependencyFailed` gating that PR adds).

Fixes three related gaps in `plan_publish`, all sharing one root cause: nothing cross-checked what `--package` selected, or what `depends_on_platforms` declared, against what actually ended up in the final plan. Found by an adversarial audit of the publish pipeline, independently re-verified three times before this fix.

- **`--only` matched by bare name only** — a Cargo crate and an npm package sharing a name (e.g. `core`) were both silently swept into a `--package core` filtered plan. Each requested name now resolves to a single, disambiguated `PackageId` via `PackageId::resolve_unique` against the full workspace membership before any filtering happens. A genuine cross-ecosystem collision reuses the existing `GraphError::AmbiguousName` and tells the caller to qualify it (`npm:core`).

- **`depends_on_platforms` was never validated** — a misconfigured platform sibling (no npm publish target) or one filtered out by `--only` let the main package publish anyway, referencing an `optionalDependencies` version that was never uploaded. Now cross-checked after filtering, allowing through only a dependency that's either present in the plan or already published (its version already tag-matches). New error: `GraphError::MissingPlatformDependency` (E121).

- **`UnknownPackage` collapsed three causes into one misleading message** — `--package` naming a real workspace package with nothing pending (not a release candidate, or no dispatchable target) returned the same "not found in workspace" message as a genuine typo. New error: `GraphError::PackageNotInPublishPlan` (E122), discriminating `NotARelease` from `NoDispatchableTarget`.

command: gh pr create --base fix-publish-order-platform-dependency-gating --head fix-package-filter-platform-dependency-validation --title "fix(graph): validate package filtering and platform dependencies against the real plan" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Stacked on #23 — depends on it merging first (this branch builds on the `depends_on_platforms`/`dependencyFailed` gating that PR adds).

Fixes three related gaps in `plan_publish`, all sharing one root cause: nothing cross-checked what `--package` selected, or what `depends_on_platforms` declared, against what actually ended up in the final plan. Found by an adversarial audit of the publish pipeline, independently re-verified three times before this fix.

- **`--only` matched by bare name only** — a Cargo crate and an npm package sharing a name (e.g. `core`) were both silently swept into a `--package core` filtered plan. Each requested name now resolves to a single, disambiguated `PackageId` via `PackageId::resolve_unique` against the full workspace membership before any filtering happens. A genuine cross-ecosystem collision reuses the existing `GraphError::AmbiguousName` and tells the caller to qualify it (`npm:core`).

- **`depends_on_platforms` was never validated** — a misconfigured platform sibling (no npm publish target) or one filtered out by `--only` let the main package publish anyway, referencing an `optionalDependencies` version that was never uploaded. Now cross-checked after filtering, allowing through only a dependency that's either present in the plan or already published (its version already tag-matches). New error: `GraphError::MissingPlatformDependency` (E121).

- **`UnknownPackage` collapsed three causes into one misleading message** — `--package` naming a real workspace package with nothing pending (not a release candidate, or no dispatchable target) returned the same "not found in workspace" message as a genuine typo. New error: `GraphError::PackageNotInPublishPlan` (E122), discriminating `NotARelease` from `NoDispatchableTarget`.

28	/// Computes the order packages must be published in.
29	///
30	/// This is a thin, purpose-named wrapper around [`toposort_impl`] (the
31	/// generic algorithm, reused as-is) rather than a generic
32	/// `DependencyResolverExt::toposort()` on a shared trait — it exists
33	/// specifically for `plan_publish` below, its only caller, and its
34	/// semantics are publish-specific, not "the one true topological sort."
35	///
36	/// Tries [`PUBLISH_ORDERING_KINDS`] first (including `Dev`, unlike cascade's
37	/// own [`CASCADE_ORDERING_KINDS`]) so a dev-dependency on a same-batch
38	/// sibling publishes in the right order. `Dev` edges are best-effort, not a
39	/// hard requirement, precisely because mutual dev-only dependencies between
40	/// two otherwise-unrelated packages are a legitimate pattern (e.g. two
41	/// crates each dev-depending on the other for cross-integration tests) —
42	/// unlike `Runtime`/`Build`/`Optional`, which must never cycle, a `Dev`
43	/// cycle must not hard-fail the whole publish plan. If including `Dev`
44	/// edges would produce a cycle, this falls back to
45	/// [`CASCADE_ORDERING_KINDS`] alone, which is guaranteed not to introduce a
46	/// *new* cycle here since it is a strict subset of the edges just proven
47	/// cyclic — accepting the original race this function exists to close for
48	/// that one pair, rather than failing the entire plan over it.
[/external_agent_tool_result]

## Summary

Stacked on #24 (touches a different function in the same file — sequenced to avoid line-number churn, not a real dependency).

`publish_order`'s fallback on a Dev-inclusive toposort cycle excluded `Dev` edges for the entire package subset, not just the packages actually forming the cycle. One legitimate Dev-only cycle anywhere in a batch (e.g. two crates mutually dev-depending on each other for cross-integration tests) silently un-ordered every other Dev-dependency in the same run — including unrelated pairs with no cycle at all — reopening the exact race (`cargo publish`'s local verification build needing a dev-dependency's new version already on crates.io) this ordering exists to close.

Fix: `toposort::cyclic_sccs` (Tarjan SCC over the full ordering-kinds-inclusive graph) plus `toposort::toposort_with_edge_filter` (a per-edge predicate instead of a static kind list — `toposort_impl` is now a thin wrapper over it, unchanged for every existing caller). `publish_order` excludes a `Dev` edge only when both its endpoints fall in the same cyclic component; every other `Dev` edge in the subset still counts. A cycle that survives with every `Dev` edge excluded is still a genuine hard failure, unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `publish_order_scopes_dev_cycle_exclusion_to_cyclic_pair_only` — the direct regression test: an unrelated Dev edge stays ordered despite a separate Dev-only cycle in the same batch
- [x] `publish_order_dev_cycle_of_three_packages` — generalizes beyond 2-node cycles
- [x] `publish_order_mixed_runtime_and_dev_cycle_excludes_only_the_dev_edge` — distinguishes a correct implementation from a subtly wrong one (SCC computed over Dev-only edges instead of the full graph); caught a bug in my own test assertion direction before landing
- [x] `cyclic_sccs_finds_only_nontrivial_components`, `cyclic_sccs_includes_self_loop` — direct unit coverage of the new helper
- [x] All 3 pre-existing Dev-cycle tests re-run unmodified

- [x] `just fmt`

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"

# Native artifact placement for CI-built platform binaries

- The shipped GitHub Action (`callisto-action`) now downloads each `callisto matrix`-driven native build's CI artifact and places it into its package directory automatically before `callisto publish` runs -- closing the gap between the build matrix and a working end-to-end release for napi-rs/maturin platform packages. No consumer-authored placement step is needed; it happens whenever `nativeMatrix` is non-empty and `publish` is enabled.
- Fixed: two packages sharing the same target platform triple no longer collapse into one `artifactName`, which previously dropped one package's build from the release silently.
- `callisto matrix --format json`'s `artifactName` values now follow napi-rs's own `<name>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]` convention (previously the raw Rust target triple), and scoped npm package names such as `@scope/addon` no longer produce an `artifactName` containing `/`, which `actions/upload-artifact` rejects.
===SEP===
---
callisto-changelog: minor
---

**Changelog entries no longer split by severity within one version**

- **Breaking:** removed `callisto_changelog::group_entries`/`GroupedEntries` — no replacement, since severity grouping no longer happens.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entries for one version now render as a single flat bullet list instead of separate `### Major Changes`/`### Minor Changes`/`### Patch Changes` sub-sections. The version heading already states the one, real applied bump — resurfacing each entry's own originally-authored severity underneath it added confusion without adding information, especially for a package bumped solely by fixed-group convergence.
[/external_agent_tool_result]

description: Open PR for cluster 3
command: gh pr create --base main --head feat-publish-skip-precheck-flag --title "feat(graph,cli): add --skip-publish-precheck to skip the redundant is_published round-trip" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

`publish_with_retry` unconditionally called `is_published` before every publish attempt. For npm this is a real subprocess + registry round-trip (`npm view`); for Cargo/PyPI it's already a no-op. On the dominant path — a freshly bumped version that's never been published — the check always returns false and buys nothing: `classify_npm_publish_output` already correctly classifies a registry-side conflict as `AlreadyPublished` from the `publish()` call itself.

Adds `PublishOrchestrator::with_skip_precheck(bool)` (default `false`, behavior unchanged) and a `--skip-publish-precheck` CLI flag. Kept opt-in rather than removing the pre-check outright — some registries' `publish()` re-runs local lifecycle scripts (npm's `prepublishOnly`/`prepack`) even on an already-published version, which the pre-check avoids.

## Test plan
- [x] `skip_precheck_true_skips_is_published_and_publishes_directly` — `is_published` never called, `publish()` called once
- [x] `skip_precheck_true_still_classifies_already_published_via_publish_call` — publish-time conflict still surfaces as `AlreadyPublished`, not a failure
- [x] `skip_precheck_default_false_preserves_existing_precheck_behavior` — unchanged default: `is_published` runs, a positive result short-circuits before `publish()`
- [x] `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib` — 421 passed
- [x] `cargo check -p callisto-cli` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `just fmt`

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"

while IFS=$'\t' read -r ARTIFACT DIR_RAW; do
  DIR="."

    DIR="$DIR_RAW"

  mkdir -p "$DIR"

[external_agent_tool_call: Bash]
description: Commit and push combined fix
command: git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(action,cli): consolidate native-artifact jq spawns, redact live-log credentials, fix Windows binary extraction

Three independent, low-risk audit findings, bundled in one PR since none touch overlapping code:

- callisto-action's native-artifact placement loop spawned 1+2N jq
  processes for an N-target matrix (one to iterate, two per entry).
  Collapsed into a single upfront jq call producing TSV. The jq
  expression explicitly forces a JSON null packageDir back to the
  literal string "null" so the existing (if odd) null-directory
  behavior isn't silently changed as a side effect of the refactor.
  Sequential fail-fast semantics (SPEC-006 AC-006) are untouched.

- callisto publish's registry commands stream stderr live to the CI
  terminal separately from the captured copy that gets redacted before
  becoming the final error message. A credential embedded in that
  stderr (e.g. a private registry URL with basic auth) was previously
  redacted only in the captured copy -- the live stream, which a CI log
  persists, was not. run_with_timeout_impl now takes a live_secrets
  list (computed from known_credential_env_values at the two real call
  sites, empty for run_quiet, which never streams live) and redacts
  both eprintln! sites before printing. The captured buffer stays raw,
  so extract_retry_after_duration/detect_auth_failure still match exact
  upstream text.

- setup-callisto correctly computes a .zip asset name for a Windows
  runner but always saved to a hardcoded .tar.gz path and ran tar -xzf
  regardless -- silently broken (masked only by no Windows release
  asset existing yet, so curl -f fails first and falls through to the
  cargo-install fallback). Added a case dispatch on $ASSET_NAME picking
  unzip vs tar -xzf and a properly-extensioned download path, with a
  defensive tar.gz fallback for any unrecognized extension.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"
git push -u origin fix-native-artifact-log-redaction-windows-zip 2>&1 | tail -15
[/external_agent_tool_call]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test for a real release run (PR #16, 2026-08-27): a plain
# `git push origin --tags` can never move an already-existing remote tag,
# so `callisto tag`'s floating major-version alias (e.g. `pkg@0`, force-moved
# LOCALLY via `git tag -f`) silently failed to reach the remote on every
# release after the first. The trailing `|| true` hid the failure entirely --
# the job reported success while the alias stayed stale.
#
# This proves the push step forces the tag update and no longer swallows a
# genuine failure.
set -u
ACTION_YML="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/action.yml"

extract_snippet() {
  sed -n '/::group::4\. Tagging Release Commits/,/::endgroup::/p' "$ACTION_YML"
}

fail=0

# The push must be forced, or an already-existing floating tag can never move.
if ! extract_snippet | grep -qE 'git push origin --tags --force'; then
  echo "FAIL: tag push step must force-push tags (git push origin --tags --force)"
  fail=1
else
  echo "PASS: tag push step forces the tag update"
fi

# The push's exit code must not be silently swallowed -- a real failure
# (auth, network, an actual conflicting tag) must fail the job, not hide.
if extract_snippet | grep -E 'git push origin --tags' | grep -q '|| true'; then
  echo "FAIL: tag push step must not swallow its own failure with '|| true'"
  fail=1
else
  echo "PASS: tag push step does not swallow its own failure"
fi

exit $fail
[/external_agent_tool_result]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test proving the native artifact placement loop lives INSIDE
# the INPUT_PUBLISH guard (SPEC-002 AC-003's "not merely somewhere after
# NATIVE_MATRIX computation" clause, and AC-004's second sentence).
#
# test_native_artifact_placement.sh extracts the loop body in isolation
# (between its own ::group::/::endgroup:: markers), so it would keep
# passing even if the loop were moved outside the guard entirely. This
# test instead extracts from the guard's own `if` line through the loop's
# ::endgroup:: -- inclusive of the guard condition itself -- so it fails
# if the loop is ever hoisted above (or the guard condition weakened
# around) that `if` line.
set -u
ACTION_YML="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/action.yml"

# The range starts at the guard's exact `if` line and ends at the FIRST
# ::endgroup:: after it -- which, if the loop is still correctly placed
# immediately inside the guard, is the loop's own closing marker. A
# missing/moved guard or loop means this range no longer captures both
# together, and the appended `fi` below then either closes nothing
# (syntax error) or closes a guard with an empty body (no gh calls even
# when INPUT_PUBLISH=true).
extract_guarded_snippet() {
  sed -n '/if \[\[ -n "\$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "\$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" \]\]; then/,/::endgroup::/p' "$ACTION_YML"
  echo "fi"
}

run_case() {
  local native_matrix="$1"
  local input_publish="$2"
  local calls_file tmp_script workdir
  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
  workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "gh() { echo \"\$*\" >> '${calls_file}'; return 0; }"
    echo "mkdir() { command mkdir \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "cd '${workdir}'"
    echo "NATIVE_MATRIX=$(printf '%q' "$native_matrix")"
    echo "GITHUB_RUN_ID=999"
    echo "INPUT_PUBLISH=$(printf '%q' "$input_publish")"
    extract_guarded_snippet
  } > "$tmp_script"
  bash "$tmp_script"
  local code=$?
  cat "$calls_file"
  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file"
  rm -rf "$workdir"
  return $code
}

fail=0
MATRIX='[{"artifactName":"pkg-a-darwin-arm64","packageDir":"packages/pkg-a"}]'

# Positive control: INPUT_PUBLISH=true must reach the loop and call gh.
out=$(run_case "$MATRIX" "true"); code=$?

  echo "FAIL positive control (INPUT_PUBLISH=true must place artifacts): code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS positive control (INPUT_PUBLISH=true places artifacts)"
fi

# entirely. If the loop were ever hoisted above this guard's `if` line,
# this case would start calling gh and fail.
out=$(run_case "$MATRIX" ""); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ -n "$out" ]]; then
  echo "FAIL AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH unset must skip placement): code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH unset skips placement)"
fi

out=$(run_case "$MATRIX" "false"); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ -n "$out" ]]; then
  echo "FAIL AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH=false must skip placement): code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS AC-003/AC-004 (INPUT_PUBLISH=false skips placement)"
fi

exit $fail

              set +e
              TAG_REPORT_JSON=$(callisto tag --plan "$PLAN_JSON" --floating-major --format json)
              TAG_EXIT=$?
              set -e
              if [[ $TAG_EXIT -ne 0 ]]; then
                echo "::error::callisto tag failed (exit $TAG_EXIT): $TAG_REPORT_JSON"
              else
                echo "$TAG_REPORT_JSON"
                # Only the floating major-version alias (e.g. `v1`) is meant to
                # move once created -- force-pushing it is correct. An
                # immutable per-version release tag must never be force-moved;
                # pushing it plainly lets git's own non-fast-forward check
                # catch a genuine conflict instead of silently overwriting it.
                IMMUTABLE_TAGS=()
                while IFS= read -r line; do
                  [[ -n "$line" ]] && IMMUTABLE_TAGS+=("$line")
                done < <(echo "$TAG_REPORT_JSON" | jq -r '.tags[] | select(.isFloatingMajor == false) | .tagName')
                FLOATING_TAGS=()
                while IFS= read -r line; do
                  [[ -n "$line" ]] && FLOATING_TAGS+=("$line")
                done < <(echo "$TAG_REPORT_JSON" | jq -r '.tags[] | select(.isFloatingMajor == true) | .tagName')

                if (( ${#IMMUTABLE_TAGS[@]} > 0 )); then
                  git push origin "${IMMUTABLE_TAGS[@]}"
                fi
                if (( ${#FLOATING_TAGS[@]} > 0 )); then
                  git push origin --force "${FLOATING_TAGS[@]}"
                fi
              fi
              echo "::endgroup::"
